account: Today has mostly followed my appointments: morning correspondence and market walk, lunch at home, town accounts, and tea with my neighbour. I have now returned to the office at 16:38 for the 16:30 appointment, where the secretary is present. During the accounts review the secretary said no figures, correspondence, or payment requests had arrived and did not know where the financial ledger was. I checked the treasury: 128 emeralds were there, and I left them untouched. The secretary offered to check the great hall tables for papers; I have not yet learned the result. The secretary also reported that the builder was seeking the innkeeper about supplies. That may be ordinary business; I do not know what supplies or purpose were involved. At tea, my neighbour mentioned vague talk of lights and some change near the bridge or port, but explicitly had no concrete details. This is the only potentially unusual report, and I cannot yet say whether there is work underway, who is involved, or what it is for. I should ask the secretary whether any planned work is known rather than treating the rumour as fact. Bread appears to be ordinary market business: I bought fresh bread, shared a loaf at tea, and my neighbour said the baker intended to stock the market today. Earlier townsfolk said the baker had carried a sack of bread at the inn; that alone does not establish anything unusual.
